Hi Tessa / Laura —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can advance procurement:

- Scope: We want to confirm the controls for handling PII when we route inference requests originating in APAC, with failover to EU/US only under the scenarios you outlined.
- Specific asks:
  1) A short table that maps data type (PII / de-identified / metadata) to residency behavior (store in-region / replicate / ephemeral-only).
  2) Logging and audit controls: what is captured (request metadata vs. full payload), retention defaults, and admin access model.
  3) Cross-region failover: how state (KV cache, prefixes) is handled and whether you offer cross-region backup windows/RPO estimates.
  4) Any standard exclusions or exceptions you need in the BAA/SLA for healthcare customers.

Can you send a one-page matrix and an estimated RPO/RTO figure for APAC->EU failover? I attached the initial SOW outline so you can tie answers to the scope.

Also looping Rajiv (CTO) who will review technical QA.

Hi Emma —

Appreciate the clear summary. Attached is our region/residency matrix v1 and a short answers doc that addresses the four bullets. High-level answers up-front:

- Data classification mapping: we recommend treating direct identifiers (SSNs, MRNs, full names + contact details) as "store-in-region" when customers opt for Private or Dedicated. For Hosted, we support in-region processing + ephemeral retention (default TTL 24h) or a pinned-region option for tenant data.

- Logging/audit: Redwood captures request metadata (IP, timestamp, model, route) by default and retains logs 90 days for hosted plans. Payload logging (full request/response) is opt-in and available only under Dedicated/Private with customer-configurable retention. Admin access is role-based and audited via our control plane; we provide searchable audit logs and exportable CSVs.

- Cross-region failover and backups: our primary approach is active-passive failover with asynchronous KV snapshotting. For APAC->EU failover we typically target RPO < 5 minutes for cache prefixes and RTO of 3-6 minutes for model endpoints (depends on sequence length and concurrency). We can tighten RTO with reserved burst pools (Dedicated).

- BAA/SLA: we have standard BAA language for healthcare customers; any specific exclusion requests should be flagged early — we'll route legal through our enterprise team.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please review the attached matrix (redwood-region-matrix-v1.xlsx).
2) If that meets your needs, we can produce a signed one-pager that maps to the SOW and propose a short technical follow-up (30 min) with Ben to validate failover mechanics.

Scheduling: I have availability Thu 20th 10:00–11:30 PT or Fri 21st 08:00–10:00 PT.

Best,

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested answers for NPH (technical)

Laura / Tessa —

Copied below is the message I'll walk through if we do the technical follow-up. Main clarifications I suggest adding to the matrix:

- Cache consistency: our KV snapshots are point-in-time and shipped encrypted; we keep three recent snapshots rolling for warm-start. During failover we mount the most recent snapshot in the target region and replay any pending requests from a short-lived queue. This is why the RPO is bounded by the snapshot cadence (default 5 minutes).

- Encryption & key ownership: for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys but we can offer a hybrid envelope encryption model on request.

- Audit detail: we can surface full request hashes (not payloads) in the default logs to help with correlation without exposing PII. Payload retention and searchable payload indices are only enabled with explicit configuration and additional controls.

- Backups: long-term backups (S3) are region-scoped and encrypted; cross-region replication only occurs with explicit customer consent and configuration in the tenancy.

If you want I can draft a short one-slide diagram showing snapshot flow and failover timeline.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emma —

Short answers inline:

1) Failover trigger: our normal configuration is automated healthcheck-based failover with a configurable threshold (default: 3 consecutive probe failures over 30s). Replication is asynchronous — we perform snapshot shipping and mount in the failover region automatically as part of the health-triggered process. We do offer a manual, operator-initiated failover for planned cutovers or legal events.

2) Sanitized audit export: attached a one-page sample CSV (column headers + two redacted rows). It includes timestamp, request_id, route, model, tenant_id (hashed), event_type, and a request_hash. Payloads are not included in the sample. If you need additional columns for SIEM ingestion (user_agent, region_source_ip), we can add them.

Proposed next step: 30-min tech call with Ben to walk the snapshot flow and kick off a short security checklist. I booked a placeholder for Fri 21 Aug 09:00 PT — if that works please accept and we'll send an agenda.

Thanks —
Tessa
